title: Spin selectivity induced by non-collinear spins in Rashba wires
authors: Luciano Jacopo D'Onofrio, Maria Teresa Mercaldo, Mario Cuoco, Carmine Ortix
abstract: We report a previously overlooked general mechanism to obtain highly efficient spin selectivity in conventional time-reversal symmetric one-dimensional systems without invoking phase decoherence. We reveal that Rashba quantum wires featuring non-collinear spin states at the Fermi level inherently possess spin-selective transport properties. We show that this spin noncollinearity can be systematically designed and engineered by introducing an additional pseudospin degree of freedom - such as valley, sublattice, or orbital angular momentum - into spin-orbit coupled systems. By applying this framework to multi-subband semiconducting quantum wires and oxide nanowires, we establish a generalized route toward quantum-coherent spin selectivity up to 10 %. Our findings offer practical design principles for spin-selective transport devices.
summary: The paper reveals a general mechanism to achieve efficient spin selectivity in 1D materials by exploiting non-collinear spin states. This non-collinearity can be engineered by coupling the electron's spin with an additional internal degree of freedom, such as orbital or valley pseudospin. The findings offer practical design rules for building next-generation quantum spin transport devices.
main_problem: The research aims to establish a general mechanism for achieving highly efficient spin selectivity in conventional time-reversal symmetric one-dimensional systems without relying on phase decoherence.
main_result: Spin selectivity is shown to arise inherently when the quantum eigenstates possess non-collinear spins, which can be engineered by introducing an additional pseudospin degree of freedom like valley or orbital angular momentum.
method: The study employs theoretical analysis involving solving scattering problems through coupled spin/pseudospin Hamiltonians and calculating the net outgoing spin polarization ($ ar{S}_{	ext{out}}$).
model_or_system: The models include Rashba quantum wires, multi-subband semiconducting quantum wires (e.g., InAs nanowires), and oxide nanowires exhibiting coupled orbital and spin degrees of freedom.
key_observables: Spin selectivity ($ ar{S}_{	ext{out}}$) and the degree of noncollinearity between spins of right-moving states are key diagnostics.
important_parameters: Rashba coupling strength ($\alpha_R$), interorbital mixing terms ($c_0$, $\alpha_{OR}$), pseudospin/orbital indices ($\hat{	au}, \hat{L}$), and system geometry parameters.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the existence of pairs of states with opposite velocity expectation values, and approximations are made regarding transverse sub-band energy spacing in some models.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate Bloch sphere representations of spin polarization dependence on angles ($\alpha,  eta$), and show calculated spin evolution and net polarization for InAs nanowires and oxide nanowires as a function of coupling parameters.
paper_structure: The paper develops the mechanism theoretically by analyzing generalized 1D systems with coupled spin/pseudospin degrees of freedom. It then applies this framework to specific physical realizations, including multi-subband semiconductor wires and complex oxide heterostructures, using scattering theory.
why_interesting: This work provides concrete, tunable design principles for realizing robust quantum spin filtering effects in solid-state systems by manipulating internal symmetries (pseudospins) rather than relying on external magnetic fields or decoherence mechanisms.
